posts.text: Skip the ATS. Connect directly. For new grads, interns, and career changers, applying online can feel like shouting into a void. Your resume might never reach a human. What if you could find the exact person hiring for your dream junior tech role and connect with them before you even apply? Here's a LinkedIn hack to do just that: 1. Go to LinkedIn's search bar. 2. Type "Recruiter" or "Hiring Manager." 3. Click "All Filters." 4. Under "Keywords," add: "junior software engineer" (or your role) AND your tech stack (e.g., "Python" or "React"). 5. Apply "Location" (your target US city/state) and "Industry." 6. Filter by "People." Now you see relevant recruiters. Next, send a personalized connection request. Don't just hit connect. Mention a specific company project you admire, a recent post of theirs, or a shared connection. Briefly state your interest in junior roles and your key skill. Example: "Hi [Name], I saw your post about [Company X]'s new project. As a new grad interested in Python/data roles, I'd love to connect." This direct approach bypasses the application black hole. You build a real connection and stand out. HireMe helps you find junior roles. This helps you get noticed for them. posts.author: CareerKrafter
posts.text: If you're a 2024/2025/2026 graduate or even still in college and preparing for your first serious switch, DSA is obviously non-negotiable. A little LLD helps too. But there's something else that is increasingly becoming important: GenAI fluency. And no, I don't mean: “I used ChatGPT to write some code.” I mean actually understanding how GenAI fits into software engineering. The interesting part? Companies are increasingly looking for this in their hiring. Look at recent SDE job descriptions across companies like Amazon, Microsoft and others. You'll increasingly find GenAI/AI experience mentioned as a preferred or required skill. And this is changing the interview conversation too. You might be asked: “Have you worked with GenAI?” And that's where many candidates get stuck. Because their previous company never gave them the opportunity to work on it. And the answer isn't to randomly add “GenAI” to your resume. You need to build the experience first, understand it properly, and then position it honestly. That's exactly what we want to help with. We are opening limited slots specifically for GenAI + SDE-1 career guidance — what to learn, what to build, how to position your existing experience.
